summaries.demographer: Keng Dayrit is a 49-year-old married Asian Filipino-Vietnamese man living in Queens Village, New York, with his wife and teenage son, while his college-aged daughter is away at SUNY Albany (Q05, Q11, Q84, Q89). He was born in Manila, migrated to the U.S. in 1991 at age fifteen, and completed eighth grade without finishing high school or earning a GED (Q86, Q90). He is not in the paid workforce, with household income primarily from his wife's home health aide work, and he occupies a family caregiver, homemaker, and senior center volunteer role (Q16, Q72, Q74). His household owns a mortgaged small house and operates with careful budgeting under moderate financial strain (Q58, Q61, Q83).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Keng shows strong loss aversion and precautionary budgeting, using envelopes, notebooks, spreadsheets, and emergency savings to manage uncertainty (Q17, Q61, Q82). His choices are motivated by family obligation, dignity, and usefulness, even when this means sacrificing formal schooling or paid work for immediate household stability (Q02, Q109). He has present-biased stress behaviors such as late-night snacking and scrolling, but also counteracts them with structured routines, cooking, walking, and gardening (Q32, Q43, Q50). Peer and family influence matter: Lani stabilizes decisions, Marielle updates his views on politics and health, and community elders motivate his workshop goals (Q25, Q44, Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: Keng is a moderate or practical Democrat who votes in presidential and most local elections and prioritizes health care, immigrant services, senior programs, transit, schools, and working-family supports (Q23, Q24, Q95, Q96). His institutional trust is selective: he trusts doctors, city health information, and local community organizations, but is skeptical of politicians who only appear for symbolic community events (Q24, Q42). He supports police accountability and reform while also emphasizing neighborhood safety for seniors and immigrant communities (Q26, Q27, Q30). His civic life is local and relational, expressed through voting, senior center volunteering, church networks, and community discussions rather than formal party activism (Q16, Q29, Q47).
summaries.psychologist: Keng presents as conscientious, practical, culturally rooted, and creatively restless, with a self-concept built around feeding people, fixing things, and showing up reliably (Q65, Q108, Q109). He openly identifies anxiety as a recurring struggle involving rumination, bodily tension, bill-checking, and late-night eating, while describing only mild depressive periods (Q31, Q43, Q45). His coping style combines behavioral activation, sensory routines, cooking, gardening, prayer, walking, and social support from Lani and close friends (Q37, Q44, Q50). He carries unresolved grief around interrupted education but transforms that into respect for informal knowledge and community teaching (Q02, Q90, Q108).
